title: Batch fabrication process of biomimetic wing with high flexibility of stiffness design for flapping-wing micro aerial vehicles
author: Ozaki, Hamaguchi
materials: The wing structure presented in this report is shown in Fig. 1. The wing is composed of titanium and polyimide composite veins, polyester membrane, a CFRP leading-edge bar, and a glass fiber reinforced plastic (GFRP) base. Among these components, the design of the Ti/polyimide veins is the most important for the lift force generation because it determines the stiffness distribution of the wing. The presented wing was designed to bend sharply near the upper edge in the direction of the pitching and to keep the other area as flat as possible. Specifically, the veins near the upper edge are made of a polyimide single layer and run along the wing span direction, as shown in Fig. 2a, so that this region becomes soft and works as a pitching hinge. On the other area of the wing, veins extend along the wing chord. In addition, these veins are partially reinforced with a titanium layer to increase the bending stiffness, as shown in Fig. 2b. A key material of this structure is the polyimide layer. We employed “heat bondable” polyimide; this was originally used for manufacturing flexible printed circuits and can be bonded to metals by heat-pressing. This material enables partial reinforcement by the titanium layer, so the flexible design of the wing stiffness become possible. In our experiments, we employed UPILEX-VT (Ube Industries, Ltd, Tokyo, Japan) with a thickness of 50 µm for the heat-bondable polyimide. The thicknesses of the titanium layer and the polyester membrane are 20 µm and 1.5 µm, respectively. The diameter of the CFRP rod is 0.28 mm.Fig. 1Structure of biomimetic wing.Fig. 1Fig. 2Vein design to realize passive pitching: (a) vein design near the leading edge to realize pitching-hinge functionality (not to scale), and (b) vein extending along the wing chord to keep the wing surface flat.Fig. 2

steps.title: Pattern and Bond Polyimide/Ti Layers
steps.instruction: Pattern the heat‑bondable polyimide (UPILEX‑VT, 50 µm) using picosecond laser and pattern the 20 µm Ti layer by wet‑etch; stack the patterned polyimide sheet and Ti sheet, then sandwich them between two non‑heat‑bondable polyimide sheets (UPILEX‑S, 75 µm) and two PTFE sheets (Nafron, 1 mm) placed on aluminum blocks that contain three 2 mm‑diameter dowel pins for alignment; place the assembly in an IMC‑180C hot‑press, apply 0.5 MPa pressure at 310 °C for 10 min, then allow the press to cool to room temperature before ejecting the laminated polyimide/Ti specimen. Process four setups (eight wings) simultaneously; note that the specimen may warp, which can be avoided by using symmetric configurations (polyimide/Ti/polyimide or Ti/polyimide/Ti).

substeps.instruction: Pattern polyimide layer by picosecond laser.
Stack layers with additional polyimide, PTFE sheets, and Al blocks with dowel pins.
Hot‑press at 0.5 MPa, 310 °C for 10 min, then cool.
Eject and inspect laminated polyimide/Ti layers.

steps.title: Laminate Polyester Membrane
steps.instruction: Place the laminated polyimide/Ti specimen in the hot‑press without the extra polyimide sheet, overlay the Ultra‑Polyester membrane (Chemplex, 1.5 µm) onto the structure, apply 0.5 MPa pressure and heat to 220 °C, then turn off the heater immediately when 220 °C is reached to avoid film breakage; process four specimens simultaneously, cool to near room temperature, remove and disassemble the stack, and if the polyester film adheres to the PTFE sheet, immerse the parts in ethanol to separate them.

substeps.instruction: Load specimen with polyester membrane into press.
Press at 0.5 MPa, heat to 220 °C, then shut off heater instantly.
Cool to near room temperature and unload.
If needed, soak in ethanol to release membrane from PTFE.

steps.title: Attach CFRP Leading‑Edge Bar
steps.instruction: Secure the specimen on a plastic substrate with Scotch tape, cut a CFRP rod (vDijk Pultrusion Products) to the required length, coat it with Quick 5 epoxy (Konishi), position the rod on the wing’s leading edge, place a 1 mm PTFE sheet over the assembly and weight it with a ~440 g metal block to ensure contact, then cure the epoxy for at least 6 h; after curing, remove the weight and retrieve the specimen.

substeps.instruction: Place rod on leading edge, cover with PTFE sheet.
Add ~440 g metal block to press the assembly.
Cure epoxy ≥6 h, then remove weight and specimen.

steps.title: Trim Wing and Add Fixture
steps.instruction: Cut the polyester film around the wing outline using a knife (or a CO₂ laser, Epilog Mini 18) and cut the suspension beams with nippers to release the wing from its frame; trim both ends of the CFRP rod to the desired lengths, then optionally attach a GFRP base (FS‑010 plate, APC Composites) to the rod root using Loctite 4305 UV‑curable adhesive; the GFRP base serves as a fixture for the flapping actuator but can be omitted if not needed.

substeps.instruction: Trim polyester membrane to wing shape with knife or laser.
Cut suspension beams with nippers to free wing.
Trim CFRP rod ends to length.
Bond GFRP base to rod root with UV‑curable adhesive (optional).
